jobava.title: The f4 pawn and the e5 square
jobava.path: d4 d5 Nc3 Nf6 Bf4 e6 e3 Bd6 Nb5 Bxf4 exf4 O-O Nf3 a6 Nc3 c5
jobava.text: After ...Bxf4 exf4 your pawn on f4 controls e5 for good. Black has also traded away the bishop that guards the dark squares.
points: Put a knight on e5: d4 and f4 protect it and Black can't kick it with a pawn.
Attack with Qf3 or Qh5 and Rae1 once the knight sits on e5.
Take on c5 when Black plays ...c5 and the recapture costs Black time.

jobava.title: Opposite castling against the King's Indian
jobava.path: d4 Nf6 Nc3 g6 Bf4 Bg7 e4 d6 Qd2 O-O O-O-O c6
jobava.text: You take the whole centre, castle long, and race your pawns at Black's king. Black races on the queenside with ...b5 and ...Qa5.
points: Trade Black's king bishop with Bh6: without it the dark squares round the king are weak.
f3, g4, h4-h5: open the h-file for your rook.
Count tempi. If Black's attack is faster, Kb1 and a calm defensive move first.

caro.title: The Exchange structure
caro.path: e4 c6 d4 d5 exd5 cxd5 Bd3 Nc6 c3 Nf6 Bf4 Bg4
caro.text: Symmetrical pawns on d4 and d5. White usually aims at your king with Bd3 and Qc2; you play on the queenside.
points: Develop the light-squared bishop (...Bg4 or ...Bf5) before ...e6 locks it in.
The minority attack: ...a6, ...b5, ...b4 against White's c3 pawn creates a weakness.
Keep a knight on f6 to defend h7 against Bd3 and Qc2 ideas.

caro.title: The Advance structure
caro.path: e4 c6 d4 d5 e5 Bf5 Nf3 e6 Be2 c5
caro.text: White's e5 pawn takes space. Your target is the base of White's chain, the d4 pawn.
points: Hit d4 with ...c5, ...Nc6 and ...Qb6: three attackers on one pawn.
The knight belongs on f5 (via e7 or h6), where it also presses d4.
Don't hurry with ...f6: it weakens e6 and your king. Use it only when d4 is well covered.

kid.title: The locked centre
kid.path: d4 Nf6 c4 g6 Nc3 Bg7 e4 d6 Nf3 O-O Be2 e5 O-O Nc6 d5 Ne7
kid.text: After d5 the centre is closed. Each side attacks where its pawns point: White on the queenside, you on the kingside.
points: Move the f6 knight (to e8 or d7) to free the f-pawn, then ...f5.
Follow up with ...f4, ...g5 and ...g4: a pawn storm at White's king.
Don't defend passively on the queenside; the race is won by speed.

kid.title: Against the London
kid.path: d4 Nf6 Bf4 g6 e3 Bg7 Nf3 O-O Be2 d6 O-O c5
kid.text: Once White's bishop leaves c1, the b2 pawn has no defender and d4 is the target.
points: ...c5 and ...Qb6 hit b2 and d4 together.
...Nc6 adds a third attacker on d4.
Later the ...e5 break, prepared with ...Nbd7, opens the bishop on g7.

e4.title: The Spanish build-up
e4.path: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 Nf6 O-O Be7 Re1 b5 Bb3 d6 c3 O-O h3
e4.text: A slow, strong set-up: c3 prepares d4, h3 stops the pin, and the b3 bishop aims at Black's king.
points: Play d4 when it is prepared; keep the e4 pawn defended.
The knight walks Nbd2, Nf1, Ng3: from g3 it eyes f5.
Keep the bishop: it is your best attacker. Retreat it to c2 if it is chased.

e4.title: The Rossolimo with doubled pawns
e4.path: e4 c5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 g6 Bxc6 dxc6 d3 Bg7 h3 Nf6 Nc3 O-O Be3 b6 Qd2
e4.text: You gave the bishop to double Black's c-pawns. Black has the two bishops, so keep the position closed.
points: Trade the dark-squared bishops with Bh6; Black's king and pawns get weaker.
Closed positions favour your knights; avoid opening lines for Black's bishops.
The doubled c-pawns are a long-term target in the endgame.

italian.title: The slow Italian
italian.path: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Bc5 c3 Nf6 d3 d6 O-O a6 a4 O-O Re1 Ba7 h3 h6 Nbd2 Re8 Nf1
italian.text: No early fight: you prepare everything, then strike in the centre or on the kingside.
points: The knight travels Nbd2, Nf1, Ng3 and then to f5.
a4 stops ...b5 from chasing your bishop.
Break with d3-d4 only when your pieces are ready.

slav.title: The Slav with ...Bf5 and ...e6
slav.path: d4 d5 c4 c6 Nf3 Nf6 Nc3 dxc4 a4 Bf5 e3 e6 Bxc4 Bb4 O-O O-O
slav.text: Like the Caro-Kann: your light-squared bishop is outside the pawn chain, and your position is very solid.
points: Free your game with ...c5 or ...e5 once your pieces are out.
If White chases the bishop with Nh4, retreat to g6 and recapture towards the centre.
Watch e4: White wants to play it, so keep pressure on it with ...Bb4 and your knights.
